title: Survive the Month
goal: Build a simple budget and understand why an emergency fund matters.

cards.text: A budget is a plan for your money: what comes in, what goes out, and what is left.

voice.speak_text: A budget is a plan for your money: what comes in, what goes out, and what is left. Say next to continue.

cards.text: In your country, {group_percent}% of {who} {indicator}. In {benchmark_name}, it is {benchmark_percent}%.

voice.speak_text: In your country, {group_percent} percent of {who} {indicator}. In {benchmark_name}, it is {benchmark_percent} percent. Say next to continue.

cards.text: Pay for needs first, like food, rent and transport.

voice.speak_text: Pay for needs first, like food, rent and transport. Say next to continue.

cards.text: Which of these is a want?

voice.speak_text: Which of these is a want? A: rent. B: food. C: a new phone. Say A, B or C.
voice.correct_feedback: Correct. A new phone is a want. Needs like rent and food come first.
voice.incorrect_feedback: Not quite. The answer is C. A new phone is a want. Needs like rent and food come first.

cards.text: Write down every small spend for one week. Small costs add up quickly.

voice.speak_text: Write down every small spend for one week. Small costs add up quickly. Say next to continue.

cards.text: When your paycheck arrives, set aside savings first, then plan the rest.

voice.speak_text: When your paycheck arrives, set aside savings first, then plan the rest. Say next to continue.

cards.text: A household budget plans for food, health and school costs before anything else.

voice.speak_text: A household budget plans for food, health and school costs before anything else. Say next to continue.

cards.text: An emergency fund is money saved only for surprises, like a doctor visit. Aim for one month of needs.

voice.speak_text: An emergency fund is money saved only for surprises, like a doctor visit. Aim for one month of needs. Say next to continue.

cards.text: A budget shows you what you can spare, so you never borrow for everyday costs.

voice.speak_text: A budget shows you what you can spare, so you never borrow for everyday costs. Say next to continue.

cards.text: You earn {cur}1000 a month and your needs cost {cur}700. How much is left for savings and wants?

voice.speak_text: You earn {cur}1000 a month and your needs cost {cur}700. How much is left for savings and wants? A: {cur}300. B: {cur}700. C: {cur}1700. Say A, B or C.
voice.incorrect_feedback: Not quite. The answer is A. {cur}1000 minus {cur}700 leaves {cur}300.

options.a: So a surprise cost does not become a loan

voice.speak_text: Why keep an emergency fund? A: so a surprise cost does not become a loan. B: to spend on wants. C: because banks require it. Say A, B or C.

spoken_options.a: so a surprise cost does not become a loan

voice.correct_feedback: Correct. An emergency fund pays for surprises without borrowing.
voice.incorrect_feedback: Not quite. The answer is A. An emergency fund pays for surprises without borrowing.

cards.text: Plan needs first, track what you spend, and build an emergency fund.

voice.speak_text: Remember: plan needs first, track what you spend, and build an emergency fund. Say next to finish the lesson.
